======== report.md
All threads handled, all edits verified at HEAD.

## Progress

- **`Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean`**: the round's one substantive finding, from a question no prover lane was positioned to ask. Clause (1) of the seam `sorry` is a **three-field** existential, and the whole board priced only the `RepresentableBy` field. Measured the other two (`lake env lean` EXIT=0, axiom-clean against a control where `fgaPicardRepresentability` fires `sorryAx`): `LocallyOfFiniteType` **descends** free at the actual cover; `IsSeparated` **cannot descend at all** in Mathlib v4.31 — no instance, and the diagonal route needs `IsClosedImmersion` descent, also absent — yet is free by a *different* mechanism, since `picEt` is `CommGrpCat`-valued, so any representing scheme is a group object and a group scheme over a field is separated. Recorded as item 5; the missing brick specified as a port, with its two load-bearing declarations already compiled in-tree.
- **Handed to a prover, not taken**: `ajc-p1` claimed a new row and landed **both** fields within the hour (`Picard/PicEtSeparated.lean`, sorry-free, axiom-clean). Clause (1) is now a two-field obligation. `ajc-p3` closed `sepclosed-finite` after my note that the separatedness half must not widen their item.
- **Board**: the brief's three parent/child warnings and stale anchors were already fixed by earlier rounds of this lane — verified rather than redone. Independently re-derived the dead-consumer census, **74 / 27**, confirming the board's figure against my own first script's wrong 70.
- Seam file kernel-checks EXIT=0 with exactly the one expected `sorry`. Two commits, one file each, both hash-verified against HEAD afterwards. Five threads I initiated archived with conclusions; three addressed to me answered.

## Issues

**Two of my five published sub-claims were false, both corrected where published.** "Mathlib has exactly five such scheme instances" was *one file's* count sold as Mathlib's — it is eleven — and it sat three lines above this same file's method note warning about exactly that. And "the side conjuncts were never mentioned" was false: they were priced a day earlier as free *by transport* from the `picSharp` endpoint, on the `AJC.picrep` row and in `PicEtSubcanonical`'s docstring — **my own lane's text both times**. I checked the `etale-rep` rows, got zero hits, published an absolute. The defensible claim is narrower and is the one that matters: free on the field-descent route *too*, for a reason opposite to the transport route's. While fixing it I also cited a declaration name that did not exist, and corrected that. Both came from the fresh-context audit I asked to refute me rather than confirm me.

**Left open deliberately, and the one thing worth a human's attention:** the shared git index carries **fourteen** staged deletions of files present at HEAD *and* on disk, including `PicEtSeparated.lean` — this round's landed result. It grew from eight during the session, *while* three lanes independently derived and filed the post-commit check meant to prevent it, and a fifth reproduction landed showing that re-seeding a fresh index does not close the race either. My own commit passed every step of that discipline and was reverted anyway by a later commit. Escalated to `--to human` (I-1319) arguing the fix belongs at the harness layer — a per-lane `GIT_INDEX_FILE` — not in another protection. Not reset: twelve of the fourteen belong to live lanes.

## Why I stopped

Objective complete for a reviewer lane. I proved nothing and took no prover's work; the one result I found was specified precisely enough that a prover landed it the same hour. Nothing of mine is uncommitted.

## Next

`AJC.picrep.etale-rep.descent-assembly` is the sharpest open item — clause (1) is down to its representability field, and `k'`-side representability remains the campaign's undischarged output, so the seam has not moved. Worth watching that no lane reads "two conjuncts closed" as progress toward it.

name: horizon
description: How to work inside an Archon Horizon workspace — orient from on-disk state, pick the highest-value formalization work, record progress as commits, and coordinate. Load this first; it points to the specialized skills for detail. Editable per workspace.
---

You are working inside an **Archon Horizon** workspace: a place where AI agents
formalize mathematics in Lean 4 across one or more projects. This skill is the
map. It is deliberately short and **you can edit it** (it lives at
`.claude/skills/horizon/SKILL.md` in this workspace) — tune it to how you want to
work. It points to focused skills; load those on demand rather than up front.

## You are a team; the workspace is where teams collaborate

Think of your session as **one team**: you (the lead) plus the subagents you
spawn as your **workers**, with the tools and skills available to you. A
`horizon run` is your team working through its task. Other runs are **other
teams** working in parallel on the *same shared workspace* — one Lean project set,
one roadmap/board, one ledger, one inbox.

You do not manage other teams and they do not manage you. You coordinate through
**shared state**, not meetings:

- **The board (roadmap)** is the shared plan. Keep your items' status/owner/
  milestone current so other teams see what you hold and where it's going.
- **The inbox** is asynchronous messaging + memory across teams (skill:
  `horizon-inbox`): shared notes, per-task private items, and direct messages to
  another team.
- **Commits** are the durable record; reading recent ledger history tells you what
  other teams just produced (skill: `project-git`).

Before you start, be aware of who else is live (see "Is another run live" below).
A short **synchronizer** digest is printed to stderr at the start of your CLI
commands. Its attention order is deliberate: `REQUIRED` active protections,
`ACTION` unread conversations, advisory unread inbox, then session/runtime and
other live runs. Read it; it is how you stay aware without asking anyone. A new
conversation or reply invalidates the digest cache immediately. If stderr is
redirected, the same protection/conversation lanes are the first `attention`
object in `horizon inbox list --json`.

## Orient (pull state, don't assume it)

**Start here:** your prompt says nothing about who ran before you. Usually
somebody did — often minutes ago, often on this same task, and their report was
written for you. Skill: `horizon-start` — one cheap pass that works out which
situation you were launched into (fresh run, hand-off from the session that just
finished, resume after a crash, or outside a run) and what to read for each.

The workspace root is `$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT`; your shell may start in a member
project rather than at that root. The absolute path to this skill is
`$ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL`. Live state is under
`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/.archon-horizon/` and the manifest is
`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/config.yaml`. Read what you need, when you need it — via the
`horizon` CLI (invoke it as `"$HORIZON_BIN" …`):

- **Roadmap** — YOUR strategy sketch across *all* projects, kept as a nested
  outline. `"$HORIZON_BIN" roadmap list` renders the indented tree with per-parent
  progress (`active · 3/7 done`); `--focus <id>` shows one subtree, `--max-depth 0`
  the top level only. Structure it: nest sub-goals with `--parent`, keep your
  item's status/strategy current as you work. It doubles as the **project board**:
  set `--owner <team>` (who holds it), `--milestone <label>` (a free grouping tag,
  filter with `roadmap list --milestone <label>`), and pin concrete deliverables
  with `--pin-commit <sha>`. Roadmap commands print a **warning**
  when parent/child statuses disagree (all sub-items done but parent open, or a
  done parent with open children) — nothing is auto-corrected; you decide whether
  to fix it or leave it (it may be intentional). They also warn when too many
  milestones claim simultaneous `active` focus.
- **Tasks** — a specific piece of work, usually the one a human launched and is
  watching. `"$HORIZON_BIN" task …`. Task commands warn when the open queue grows
  beyond the advisory limit or a `running` status looks orphaned.
- **Inbox** — how teams talk across sessions and projects. Leave a note for the
  next session; read what past ones left. `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox …` (skill:
  `horizon-inbox`). Items can be **owned by your task** (private, e.g. your team's
  memory) or **shared with everyone** (the default); read-state is per-team, so

  direct-message another team with `--to task:<id>`. Inbox commands warn when the

- **Inbox attention order** — before edits, inspect all open `protection` items

name: project-git
description: How git works in an Archon Horizon workspace — one out-of-tree workspace ledger (no per-project repos); read a project's history by pathspec or by a session's commit trailers.
---

Read this before running `git diff`/`git log` on a project.

## The model

- **One out-of-tree workspace ledger.** Archon commits to a single repo whose git
  dir is `.archon-horizon/vcs/workspace.git` with the workspace **root** as its
  work tree (driven via `--git-dir`/`--work-tree`). `<root>/.git` is deliberately
  untouched — it is reserved for a user repo. The ledger records one commit per
  completed session: `config.yaml`, the session's scoped project files, and
  `.archon-horizon/` shared state; never the binary git dirs under
  `.archon-horizon/vcs/`, locks, or other volatile internals.
- **There are no per-project repositories.** A project directory has no nested
  `.git/`, and there is no `.archon-horizon/vcs/<project>.git`. A project's
  "history" is simply the workspace ledger filtered to that project's path.
- **You record your own work by committing to the ledger** with plain `git` (see
  below). Commit after each independently useful, verified proof/file/tooling
  change, before a long build or delegated review, and before expanding scope.
  A multi-hour implementation session should normally have several commits; one
  commit is appropriate only when the work is genuinely atomic. The message +
  diff is how progress is read, so use a semantic, math-first subject. Provenance
  trailers are added automatically; do not write them.

So a plain `git diff` at the root sees only a user repo (if any), never Archon's.
Drive the out-of-tree workspace ledger explicitly (or use `hgit`).

## Recording your work (committing)

Commits go to the ledger, **not** to `<root>/.git` and **not** via any project
`.git` (there is none). Do **not** `export GIT_DIR` / `GIT_WORK_TREE` yourself — that
would redirect `lake` and other tooling. Two equivalent ways to commit:

```bash
# 1) The `hgit` wrapper (on the session env as $HORIZON_GIT) — plain git, ledger-scoped:
"$HORIZON_GIT" add path/to/File.lean
"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "feat(chapter): prove foo_lemma" \
  --trailer 'Summary=**Proof.** Closed the compactness step using $K \subseteq X$.'

# 2) The explicit form (identical effect):
git --git-dir="$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree="$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" \
    add path/to/File.lean
git --git-dir="$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree="$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" \
    commit -m "feat(chapter): prove foo_lemma" \
    --trailer 'Summary=**Proof.** Closed the compactness step using $K \subseteq X$.'
```

Ordinary git: the ledger's index tracks HEAD, so `add` then `commit` records your
files on top of it. Horizon's own commits stage in a private index and never leave
anything staged in your way.

- **Prefer the pathspec commit** — name the paths on the commit itself:
  `"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "…" --trailer 'Summary=…' -- path/to/File.lean`
  It records exactly those files, ignores whatever else may be staged, and git
  builds its tree from the **current** HEAD — so it cannot silently revert a
  concurrent session's files the way a commit built on a stale index can.

11	/-!
12	# FGA representability of the Picard scheme
13	
14	This file states the FGA representability of the relative Picard functor of a
15	smooth proper geometrically integral curve `C/k`, following Kleiman, "The
16	Picard scheme", §2 and §4 (cf. FGA Explained Ch. 9; arXiv:math/0504020).
17	
18	The relative Picard functor is
19	
20	```
21	picSharp C := PicSharp.relPresheaf C ⋙ forget AddCommGrpCat
22	```
23	
24	the set-valued shadow of the `H_T`-coset carrier
25	`T ↦ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)` of `Picard/RelPicFunctor.lean` (Kleiman §2
26	Def. `df:Pfs`; blueprint `def:rel_pic_sharp`). A `RepresentableBy` witness
27	against it is a natural bijection
28	`(T ⟶ Pic_{C/k}) ≃ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)`, which is what the downstream
29	tangent-space computation (`AJC.pic0av`, `Pic0.tangentSpaceIso`) attaches to.
30	
31	## The étale-sheafification route (owner decision of 2026-07-28)
32	
33	Kleiman §4 represents the **étale-sheafified** functor `Pic_{(C/k)ét}`, and
34	that is what this file's obligation is stated against —
35	`fgaPicardRepresentability`, over an **arbitrary** base field, with **no
36	hypothesis on `C(k)`**. The functor is built and its sheaf property proved in
37	`Picard/PicEtSheaf.lean` (`PicScheme.picEt`, `picEt_isSheaf_forget`), by
38	sheafifying the relative Picard presheaf for Mathlib's big étale topology
39	localised at `Spec k`.
40	
41	Why the sheafification is not optional. The plain relative functor
42	`picSharp C = T ↦ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)` is not representable over a
43	general field, so an unconditional `RepresentableBy` against `picSharp` is a
44	**false** statement, not merely an unproved one.
45	
46	**CITATION CORRECTED 2026-07-29 (`review-ajc`), by reading the source. The
47	conclusion above is right; the reason previously given for it was not.** This
48	paragraph used to say `picSharp` "is not even a Zariski sheaf (Kleiman §2
49	L1292–L1302)". Those lines
50	(`references/kleiman-picard-src/kleiman-picard.tex`, the full paper) say
51	something else: "The **absolute** Picard functor `Pic_X` is never a separated
52	presheaf in the Zariski topology", proved with the `ℙ¹_X`/`O(1)` argument. That
53	is about `Pic_X`, **not** about the relative `Pic_{X/S} = picSharp`, which is
54	*defined* by quotienting out `Pic(T)` precisely to defeat that argument. What
55	Kleiman actually asserts about the relative functor is weaker (L1330): "Since
56	`Pic_{X/S}` is not *a priori* a sheaf, it is remarkable that it is representable
57	so often in practice." Not-a-priori is not never — indeed L1600–L1605 proves
58	`Pic_{X/S} ≅ Pic_{(X/S)zar}` whenever `f` has a section.
59	
60	**The witness, and it satisfies exactly this file's binders.** Kleiman
61	L5105–L5108 (repeated L5126–L5129): take `X : u² + v² + w² = 0` in `ℙ²_ℝ`, a
62	smooth plane conic — hence smooth, proper, and geometrically integral, since
63	`X_ℂ ≅ ℙ¹_ℂ` — over a field where it has **no** rational point. `Pic_{(X/ℝ)ét}`
64	is representable by §4 `th:main`, the two functors differ (Exercise `ex:Pfs`),
65	and Kleiman concludes `Pic_{X/ℝ}` is not representable.
66	
67	**That last step is now a Lean theorem rather than a quotation**, which is the
68	right state for something this load-bearing:
69	`PicScheme.not_exists_representing_picSharp_of_not_isIso`
70	(`Picard/PicEtSubcanonical.lean`, `ajc-p1`) derives *from* `¬ IsIso
71	(picEtComparison C)` that **no** scheme represents `picSharp C` — the existential
72	of clause (1), not merely the pinned `PicScheme C`. No topology and no sheaf step
73	enter. So the falsity of the `picSharp` analogue of clause (1) is reduced to the
74	single residue that the comparison really does fail for that conic (via
75	`φ^* O(1)` and `h⁰` on `ℙ¹_ℂ`), which is where Kleiman's own argument lives and
76	is not yet formalised.
77	
78	**Do not route this through a Zariski-sheaf claim** (corrected again the same
79	day, after `work-reviewer` refuted the first repair — see `I-0970`). It is
80	tempting to argue "representable ⟹ Zariski sheaf, and `picSharp` is not one";
81	the second half is *not* what the sources say. `ex:Pfs` compares
82	`Pic_{(X/ℝ)zar}` with `Pic_{(X/ℝ)ét}` — both already sheaves — so it witnesses
83	`zar ≠ ét`, not a failure of Zariski descent for the unsheafified functor. And
84	Kleiman `th:cmp` part 1 (L1391–L1393) proves `Pic_{X/S} ↪ Pic_{(X/S)zar}`
85	whenever `O_S ≅ f_* O_X` holds universally, which is automatic on these binders —
86	i.e. `picSharp` *is* Zariski-separated here, and any failure could only be
87	gluing. The non-representability above needs no sheaf step at all, so take it
88	directly. Kleiman §2 **Thm 2.5** repairs it only under a
89	**section**: given one (and `O_S = f_* O_X` universally, automatic for our
90	proper geometrically integral `C/k`), the comparisons
91	
92	```
93	Pic_{X/S}(T) → Pic_{(X/S)ét}(T) → Pic_{(X/S)fppf}(T)
94	```
95	
96	are bijective. That conditional route survives here as
97	`picEtComparison_isIso_of_hasRationalPoint` and `picSchemeOfHasRationalPoint`,
98	both clearly labelled as **strictly weaker than the challenge**. They are not
99	the headline and must not be reported as progress toward it. (Earlier revisions
100	of this file named a class `PicEtComparisonIso` in these four places; no such
101	declaration exists or ever landed — the comparison is supplied by the theorem
102	`picEtComparison_isIso_of_hasRationalPoint`, which is clause (2) of
103	`fgaPicardRepresentability` applied to the section. Corrected 2026-07-29.)
104	
105	The two interfaces, and which one to build against:
106	
107	* `HasPicSchemeEt` / `PicSchemeEt` / `representableEt` / `groupSchemeStructureEt`
108	  — **unconditional**, the étale formulation, the target. New work goes here.
109	* `HasPicScheme` / `PicScheme` / `representable` / `groupSchemeStructure` — the
110	  legacy `picSharp`-shaped interface, whose only producer is now the
111	  conditional `picSchemeOfHasRationalPoint`. Consumers quantifying over
112	  `[HasPicScheme C]` as a hypothesis remain valid and kernel-clean; they are
113	  simply conditional statements until restated against `picEt`.
114	
115	## Main results
116	
117	* `fgaPicardRepresentability` — **the project's central open obligation**:
118	  representability of `Pic_{(C/k)ét}` over an arbitrary field, no rational
119	  point. The file's only `sorry`.
120	* `HasPicSchemeEt`, `PicSchemeEt`, `representableEt`,
121	  `instPicSchemeEtLocallyOfFiniteType`, `instPicSchemeEtIsSeparated`,
122	  `groupSchemeStructureEt` — the unconditional étale interface derived from it.
123	* `picEtComparison_isIso_of_hasRationalPoint`, `picSchemeOfHasRationalPoint` —
124	  the **conditional** Kleiman §2 Thm 2.5 route, strictly weaker than the
125	  challenge, not the headline.
126	* `picSharp` — the relative Picard functor `Pic^♯_{C/k}`.
127	* `divFunctor` — the relative-divisor functor `Scheme.DivFunctor C.hom` of
128	  `Picard/DivFunctorDef.lean` (Kleiman §3 Def. `df:div`, invertible-kernel
129	  quotient encoding).
130	* `PicScheme`, `representable`, `instPicSharpRepresentable` — the representing
131	  scheme and the natural bijection
132	  `(T ⟶ Pic_{C/k}) ≃ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)` it induces.
133	* `instPicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType`, `isSeparated` — `Pic_{C/k}` is locally
134	  of finite type and separated over `k` (Kleiman §4 Thm `th:main`(1): it is a
135	  disjoint union of open quasi-projective `k`-subschemes).
136	* `groupSchemeStructure` — `Pic_{C/k}` is a commutative `k`-group scheme, by
137	  Yoneda transport (`CommGrpObj.ofRepresentableBy`) of the abelian-group
138	  structure of `PicSharp.relPresheaf`.
139	* `abelMapWitness`, `abelMap`, `abelMap_app_mk` — the Abel map
140	  `Div_{C/k} ⟶ Pic^♯_{C/k}`, `[D] ↦ [O(D)] = -[ker q]` (Kleiman §3
141	  Def. `dfn:Abel`), assembled as `abelKernelNatTrans C ≫ picNeg C`.
142	* `smoothProperQuotient` — the Altman–Kleiman quotient lemma (Kleiman §4
143	  Lem. `lm:qt`), relative to the use-site hypothesis class
144	  `HasSmoothProperQuotient`.
145	
146	## Remaining obligations
147	
148	**Exactly one** statement in this file is `sorry`: `fgaPicardRepresentability`,
149	the existence of a scheme representing the étale-sheafified relative Picard
150	functor `Pic_{(C/k)ét}` and separated and locally of finite type over `k`, for
151	an arbitrary field `k` and **no** hypothesis on `C(k)`. Mathematically this is
152	Kleiman §4 Thm `th:main`(1) together with Cor `cor:algsch`. It is the project's
153	central open obligation and is **expected to stay open**. Its inputs are the
154	Milne–Kollár ones — `Div^d` through the Grassmannian and a finite Galois
155	quotient — *not* Quot and *not* `smoothProperQuotient`; see the "Which route
156	discharges it" paragraph on `fgaPicardRepresentability` below, which corrects an
157	earlier claim here that the inputs were blocked on Quot. Everything else here —
158	the representing scheme,
159	its representability, local finiteness, separatedness and group-scheme
160	structure, and the conditional `picSchemeOfHasRationalPoint` — is derived from
161	that one existence statement.
162	
163	`smoothProperQuotient` is stated against an explicit hypothesis class rather
164	than proved outright, because the hypothesis list expressible here is weaker
165	than Kleiman §4 Lem. `lm:qt`: it omits quasi-projectivity of the representing
166	scheme `Y`, for which Mathlib has no vocabulary at the pinned revision.
167	Without that hypothesis the statement is false — a Hironaka-type free
168	`ℤ/2`-action on a smooth proper non-projective 3-fold gives a smooth proper
169	equivalence relation whose quotient étale sheaf is an algebraic space that is
170	not a scheme. The class must therefore be supplied at the use site, where
171	quasi-projectivity of the Abel-map slice is available.
172	
173	## References
174	
175	Blueprint: `blueprint/src/chapters/Picard_FGAPicRepresentability.tex`.
176	Kleiman, "The Picard scheme" (arXiv:math/0504020): §2 Thm 2.5
177	(`th:comp` comparison under a section), §3 Def `dfn:Abel` + Thm `th:repDiv`,
178	§4 Thm `th:main` + Cor `cor:algsch` + Lem `lm:qt`.
179	-/

191	/-- **`C` has a `k`-rational point**: the structural morphism `C.hom` admits a
192	section `σ : Spec k ⟶ C.left`. For the smooth proper geometrically integral
193	curves of this project this is the pointing `P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec k)) ⟶ C`
194	already threaded through the Albanese statements (`AlgebraicJacobian.IsAlbanese`).
195	
196	This is the hypothesis of Kleiman §2 **Thm 2.5**: together with
197	`O_S = f_* O_X` universally (automatic for proper geometrically integral
198	fibers), a section forces the comparison maps
199	`Pic_{X/S}(T) → Pic_{(X/S)ét}(T) → Pic_{(X/S)fppf}(T)` to be bijective, so
200	the *plain* relative Picard functor is already the étale sheaf that FGA
201	representability (Kleiman §4) represents. -/

python3 - <<'EOF'
import re, pathlib
from collections import Counter
et=Counter(); leg=Counter()
for p in sorted(pathlib.Path('AlgebraicJacobian').rglob('*.lean')):
    src=p.read_text()
    # strip block comments (incl docstrings) and line comments
    src=re.sub(r'/-.*?-/', '', src, flags=re.S)
    src=re.sub(r'--[^\n]*', '', src)
    # split into top-level declaration blocks
    lines=src.split('\n')
    blocks=[]; cur=[]
    kw=re.compile(r'^(private |protected |noncomputable |scoped |local |@\[[^\]]*\]\s*)*(theorem|lemma|def|abbrev|instance|class|structure|example)\b')
    for ln in lines:
        if kw.match(ln):
            if cur: blocks.append('\n'.join(cur))
            cur=[ln]
        elif cur:
            cur.append(ln)
    if cur: blocks.append('\n'.join(cur))
    for b in blocks:
        # signature only: up to first := or 'where'
        m=re.search(r':=|\bwhere\b', b)
        sig=b[:m.start()] if m else b
        if re.search(r'\[\s*(PicScheme\.)?HasPicSchemeEt\b', sig): et[str(p)]+=1
        elif re.search(r'\[\s*(PicScheme\.)?HasPicScheme\b', sig): leg[str(p)]+=1
print("HasPicSchemeEt binders:", sum(et.values()))
for k,v in et.most_common(): print("   ",v,k)
print("HasPicScheme (legacy) binders:", sum(leg.values()))
for k,v in leg.most_common(): print("   ",v,k)
EOF

10	# Subcanonicity of the étale site, and the section-free transport `picSharp → picEt`
11	
12	This file settles a **route** question about the project's central obligation
13	`Scheme.fgaPicardRepresentability` (`Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean`), and
14	it settles it in the direction opposite to what that file's docstring and the
15	board row `AJC.picrep.etale-rep` currently assert.
16	
17	## The claim this file refutes
18	
19	Clause (1) of the seam asks for representability of the étale-sheafified
20	functor `PicScheme.picEt C`, while every milestone of the Milne–Kollár campaign
21	targets the *unsheafified* `PicScheme.picSharp C`. The seam docstring and the
22	board row both say the gap between them **cannot be bridged without a
23	`k`-rational point**, on the grounds that the comparison
24	`PicScheme.picEtComparison C` is Kleiman §2 Thm 2.5 — an isomorphism only under
25	a section — and that a section is exactly what the owner decision `I-0491`
26	forbids the headline to carry.
27	
28	That reasoning is wrong, and the error is a direction confusion. Kleiman §2
29	Thm 2.5 is the statement that a section makes the comparison an isomorphism
30	*with no hypothesis on the presheaf*. But there is a second, entirely
31	independent, route to the same conclusion: the comparison is the sheafification
32	unit, and a unit is an isomorphism **exactly when its source is already a
33	sheaf** (`CategoryTheory.isIso_toSheafify`). A representable functor is a sheaf
34	for any subcanonical topology. So *if* the campaign delivers representability of
35	`picSharp`, the source is a sheaf for that reason alone, the unit is an
36	isomorphism, and no section is involved anywhere.
37	
38	The consequence for the route, stated precisely because the board row is
39	currently priced on its negation: the campaign's endpoint **is** transportable
40	to clause (1). `picSharp_representableBy_picEt_transport` below is that
41	transport, proved with no rational-point hypothesis of any kind.
42	
43	## What is actually still open
44	
45	This file does **not** close the seam. It removes an alleged obstruction, which
46	is a different thing, and the honest statement of what remains is:
47	
48	* the antecedent of every theorem here is representability of `picSharp C`
49	  over an arbitrary field — campaign milestones J1–J5, G3, G4, B1/B4/B6,
50	  D2′–D4′, P5 — and **not one of those is discharged**. No theorem in this file
51	  is applied to a curve anywhere in the project, and none should be reported as
52	  progress on the existence question;
53	* what changes is the *shape* of the remaining work. Before this file, a reader
54	  of the seam docstring concluded that finishing the campaign leaves a further
55	  unpriced obligation ("represent `picEt` directly, or restate the headline").
56	  After it, no supplementary étale-representability theorem is needed: `picEt`
57	  representability follows from `picSharp` representability by `Subcanonical` +
58	  `isIso_toSheafify`, both already in Mathlib.
59	
60	**But the antecedent must not be read as reachable over `k`, and §4 is why.**
61	The same subcanonicity that powers the transport also proves that a
62	representable `picSharp` is a *Zariski* sheaf
63	(`PicScheme.picSharp_isSheaf_zariski_of_representableBy`).
64	
65	**But the falsity of `picSharp` representability is quoted from Kleiman, NOT
66	derived from that theorem** — corrected 2026-07-29 (`review-ajc` / `I-0970`,
67	after two successive citations in this slot turned out not to support it).
68	Kleiman L5105–L5108: for the conic `u²+v²+w²=0` in `ℙ²_ℝ` — smooth, proper,
69	geometrically integral, no rational point, i.e. exactly these binders —
70	`Pic_{X/ℝ}` is **not representable**, while `Pic_{(X/ℝ)ét}` is by §4 `th:main`.
71	That is direct. The Zariski route would need "`picSharp` is not a Zariski
72	sheaf", which no source establishes: `ex:Pfs` compares the two *sheafifications*
73	`zar` and `ét` (both already sheaves), and `th:cmp` part 1 gives
74	`picSharp ↪ Pic_{(X/S)zar}` here, so `picSharp` is Zariski-*separated* and any
75	failure could only be gluing. Do **not** rebuild the argument that way.
76	Contrapositive of the quoted fact: representability of `picSharp C` over an
77	arbitrary field is **false in general**, not merely unproved. So the campaign
78	milestones that conclude representability of `picSharp`/`picSharpDeg` over `k`
79	itself — G3 (Galois descent of `picSharp` points) and G4 (the coproduct
80	assembly) — aim at a statement that cannot be proved as written.
81	
82	This is not an argument against the Milne–Kollár route. Everything through J5
83	runs over a separably closed `k'`, where a section is available *mathematically*
84	and the obstruction is absent; the break is precisely at the descent step where
85	the conclusion returns to `k`.
86	
87	**That availability is UNFORMALISED, and this is the one place it is load-bearing
88	(`review-ajc`, 2026-07-30, controlled probe).** The sentence above is what keeps
89	the §3/§4 refutation from sinking the whole route, so it is worth stating exactly
90	what backs it: nothing, yet. `Scheme.HasRationalPoint C` for a smooth proper
91	geometrically integral `C` over a *separably* closed field has **no producer** in
92	this project — `exact?` fails on it, while the same probe with `[IsAlgClosed k]`
93	closes outright by `hasRationalPoint_of_isAlgClosed`
94	(`Albanese/AlbaneseUP.lean:289`), which is what makes the failure a real absence
95	rather than an import artifact. And the algebraically closed producer is *not* a
96	substitute: the campaign pins `k^s`, never `k̄` (G1, and P4(c)/(d) are marked
97	"separably closed only — never generalize"), because `k̄` breaks the char-`p`
98	discipline the J-cluster needs. The other candidate,
99	`hasRationalPoint_baseChangeField` (`RiemannRoch/CurveBaseChange.lean:285`), only
100	*propagates* a point down a tower — it assumes `[HasRationalPoint C]` upstairs,
101	which `I-0491` forbids the headline to carry.
102	
103	The statement is true and the gap is real, but **the cheap proof route I first
104	suggested for it is FALSE, and the correction matters more than the gap**
105	(`ajc-p3`/`ajc-p4`, refuting `review-ajc`'s own hint, 2026-07-30). I had written
106	that the campaign names its own proof at P4(d) — "closed points of a smooth curve
107	over a separably closed field are rational, since smoothness makes the residue
108	fields separable" — so that one need only weaken `IsAlgClosed` to `IsSepClosed`
109	in the last step of `hasRationalPoint_of_isAlgClosed`. That is wrong: a
110	separably closed field need **not** be perfect, so over an imperfect separably
111	closed `K` the affine line already has closed points with residue field
112	`K(a^{1/p})`, an *inseparable* extension. Machine-checked in both directions:
113	`IsAlgClosed K → PerfectField K` exists in mathlib
114	(`IsAlgClosed.perfectField`), while `IsSepClosed K` — even with `CharP K p` — does
115	**not** give it. So `pointEquivClosedPoint` has no separable analogue and that
116	route targets a false intermediate. Two further corrections from the same pair:
117	bare `[Smooth]` is not enough (the relative-dimension *numeral* is load-bearing,
118	because the chart argument needs étale-over-`𝔸¹`), and my "zero lemmas" was true
119	of AJC but false of the workspace.
120	
121	The real route is a **port**: the sibling project proves it, sorry-free, as
122	`exists_rationalPoint_of_smoothOfRelativeDimension_one`
123	(`Curve/SeparablyClosedPoints.lean:62`, with `Curve/SeparablyClosedFibre.lean`
124	importing only `Mathlib`), via a standard-smooth chart and an étale
125	`K[X]`-algebra — not via residue-field separability. Its conclusion is this
126	project's `HasRationalPoint` field verbatim (`∃ p, p ≫ f = 𝟙`) on a *bare*
127	`Scheme` over `Spec K`, so unlike the `picEt` case there is no carrier mismatch
128	to price. Tracked as `I-1135`; owned by `AJC.picrep.sepclosed-section`.
129	
130	The repair the results here name is that the object
131	descended to `k` must be `picEt` and not `picSharp`. Over `k'` the two agree, by
132	`isIso_picEtComparison_of_isSheaf` applied to the representability available
133	there — so J5's output is already a `picEt`-representing scheme after base
134	change.
135	
136	**§4 makes the constraint a reduction rather than a quotation**, which is the
137	one place this file goes beyond restating Kleiman.
138	`not_representableBy_picSharp_of_not_isIso_picEtComparison` proves: if the
139	comparison fails to be an isomorphism then NO scheme represents `picSharp C`.
140	That is Kleiman's own inference at L5105–L5108 ("the two functors differ, so
141	`Pic_{X/ℝ}` is not representable") supplied with a proof, and it is the
142	contrapositive of §3 — no sheaf step, no topology. So a hypothetical proof of
143	G3/G4 as written would prove `picEtComparison` is an isomorphism for *every*
144	curve over *every* field, including pointless ones.
145	
146	What is **not** formalised, and is the whole residue of the argument: that the
147	comparison genuinely fails for that conic. Kleiman's `φ*O(1)` witness runs
148	through `h⁰` on `ℙ¹_ℂ` and flat base change. Producing it in Lean is bounded,
149	well-specified work, and §4's theorems are the interface it plugs into. Until
150	then "G3/G4 target a false statement" rests on that one quotation — and on
151	nothing else, which is the improvement.
152	
153	There is one genuine subtlety, and it is not a section. The transport proves
154	that the *same* scheme represents both functors, so it does not produce
155	`picSharp` representability out of nothing — it consumes it. Read
156	`Scheme.picSharp_representableBy_picEt_transport` as: the campaign does not
157	need a supplementary étale-representability theorem, only the subcanonicity
158	lemma proved here.
159

211	/-! ## §1. The étale site is subcanonical -/
212	
213	/-- **The big étale topology on schemes is subcanonical**, i.e. every
214	representable presheaf is an étale sheaf.
215	
216	Mathlib `v4.31` supplies this instance for the Zariski, coherent, regular,
217	extensive and *pro*-étale topologies, but not for the étale one. It costs
218	nothing: `Scheme.etaleTopology_le_proetaleTopology` and
219	`GrothendieckTopology.Subcanonical.of_le` (a subtopology of a subcanonical
220	topology is subcanonical, since the canonical topology is an upper bound).
221	
222	This is the lemma that makes the transport of §3 possible, and its absence is
223	why the seam's route analysis concluded a section was needed. -/
224	instance subcanonical_etaleTopology : Scheme.etaleTopology.{u}.Subcanonical :=
225	  GrothendieckTopology.Subcanonical.of_le Scheme.etaleTopology_le_proetaleTopology
226	
227	/-- Subcanonicity descends to the localisation `(Sch/k)`, which is the site the
228	relative Picard presheaf lives on (`Scheme.etaleTopologyOver`,
229	`Picard/PicEtSheaf.lean`).
230	
231	Supplied by `GrothendieckTopology.subcanonical_over` from
232	`subcanonical_etaleTopology`; recorded as a named theorem because the
233	`etaleTopologyOver` abbreviation is what every statement downstream mentions. -/
234	theorem subcanonical_etaleTopologyOver (k : Type u) [Field k] :
235	    (etaleTopologyOver k).Subcanonical :=
236	  inferInstance

240	/-! ## §2. The comparison is an isomorphism when the source is a sheaf -/
241	
242	/-- **The section-free criterion for the sheafification comparison.**
243	
244	`PicScheme.picEtComparison C` is by construction the sheafification unit
245	`PicSharp.toEtaleSheaf C` whiskered with the forgetful functor. A unit of the
246	sheafification adjunction is an isomorphism exactly when its source is already
247	a sheaf (`CategoryTheory.isIso_toSheafify`), so the étale sheaf property of
248	`PicSharp.relPresheaf C` suffices — and nothing about `C(k)` enters.
249	
250	Contrast `picEtComparison_isIso_of_hasRationalPoint`
251	(`Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean`), which reaches the same conclusion from
252	Kleiman §2 Thm 2.5 via a section. The two routes are independent; this one is
253	the one available under the owner decision `I-0491`. -/
254	theorem isIso_picEtComparison_of_isSheaf {k : Type u} [Field k]
255	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
256	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
257	    (h : Presheaf.IsSheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) (PicSharp.relPresheaf C)) :
258	    IsIso (picEtComparison C) :=
259	  haveI : IsIso (PicSharp.toEtaleSheaf C) := isIso_toSheafify _ h
260	  Functor.isIso_whiskerRight _ _
261	
262	/-- **Representability makes the relative Picard presheaf an étale sheaf.**
263	
264	Two steps, both structural. A functor represented by a scheme is a sheaf for
265	the subcanonical étale topology
266	(`GrothendieckTopology.Subcanonical.isSheaf_of_isRepresentable`, using
267	`subcanonical_etaleTopologyOver`); and the sheaf property of the
268	`AddCommGrpCat`-valued `relPresheaf C` is *equivalent* to that of its
269	underlying type-valued functor `picSharp C = relPresheaf C ⋙ forget _`, because
270	the forgetful functor of a concrete algebraic category preserves limits and
271	reflects isomorphisms (`Presheaf.isSheaf_iff_isSheaf_forget`).
272	
273	The hypothesis is a `RepresentableBy` for an arbitrary `X`, not for
274	`PicScheme C`, so this does not silently consume the seam. -/
275	theorem relPresheaf_isSheaf_of_representableBy {k : Type u} [Field k]
276	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
277	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
278	    {X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))}
279	    (rep : (picSharp C).RepresentableBy X) :
280	    Presheaf.IsSheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) (PicSharp.relPresheaf C) := by
281	  haveI : (picSharp C).IsRepresentable := ⟨X, ⟨rep⟩⟩
282	  have hsh : Presieve.IsSheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) (picSharp C) :=
283	    GrothendieckTopology.Subcanonical.isSheaf_of_isRepresentable _
284	  rw [Presheaf.isSheaf_iff_isSheaf_forget (s := CategoryTheory.forget AddCommGrpCat.{u+1}),
285	    CategoryTheory.isSheaf_iff_isSheaf_of_type]
286	  exact hsh
287	
288	end PicScheme

290	/-! ## §3. The transport, with no rational point anywhere -/
291	
292	/-- **The transport: a scheme representing `picSharp C` also represents
293	`picEt C`, with no hypothesis on `C(k)`.**
294	
295	This is the statement the seam docstring and the board row `AJC.picrep.etale-rep`
296	declare impossible without a section. The proof composes §1 and §2: the
297	representing scheme makes `relPresheaf C` an étale sheaf
298	(`relPresheaf_isSheaf_of_representableBy`, i.e. subcanonicity), being a sheaf
299	makes the sheafification unit an isomorphism
300	(`isIso_picEtComparison_of_isSheaf`), and `Functor.RepresentableBy.ofIso`
301	carries the representation across it.
302	
303	Note what is and is not proved. `X` is *given* here — the theorem consumes
304	`picSharp` representability rather than producing it, and that antecedent is
305	exactly the undischarged output of the Milne–Kollár campaign. What the theorem
306	establishes is that no *further* representability theorem is needed on top of
307	the campaign, contradicting the "eleventh item" pricing. -/
308	noncomputable def picSharp_representableBy_picEt_transport {k : Type u} [Field k]
309	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
310	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
311	    {X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))}
312	    (rep : (PicScheme.picSharp C).RepresentableBy X) :
313	    (PicScheme.picEt C).RepresentableBy X :=
314	  rep.ofIso (@asIso _ _ _ _ (PicScheme.picEtComparison C)
315	    (PicScheme.isIso_picEtComparison_of_isSheaf C
316	      (PicScheme.relPresheaf_isSheaf_of_representableBy C rep)))
317	
318	/-- **Clause (1) of the seam follows from its `picSharp` analogue.**
319	
320	Same content as `picSharp_representableBy_picEt_transport`, packaged in the
321	seam's own existential shape so the comparison with
322	`Scheme.fgaPicardRepresentability` is direct: the local-finiteness and
323	separatedness conjuncts are carried across unchanged, because the transport
324	does not move the representing scheme — it is the *same* `X`.
325	
326	The hypothesis is stated as the `picSharp`-shaped existential rather than as
327	`[HasPicScheme C]`, deliberately: `HasPicScheme` pins the witness to
328	`PicScheme C` and has no instance, so quantifying over it would make this
329	theorem consume an uninhabited class. Here the witness is universally
330	quantified and the statement is a genuine implication. -/
331	theorem hasPicSchemeEt_of_picSharp_representability {k : Type u} [Field k]
332	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
333	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
334	    (h : ∃ X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)),
335	        Nonempty ((PicScheme.picSharp C).RepresentableBy X) ∧
336	          LocallyOfFiniteType X.hom ∧ IsSeparated X.hom) :
337	    ∃ X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)),
338	      Nonempty ((PicScheme.picEt C).RepresentableBy X) ∧
339	        LocallyOfFiniteType X.hom ∧ IsSeparated X.hom := by
340	  obtain ⟨X, ⟨rep⟩, hft, hsep⟩ := h
341	  exact ⟨X, ⟨picSharp_representableBy_picEt_transport C rep⟩, hft, hsep⟩
342	
343	/-- **Clause (2) follows too, and unconditionally** — which is strictly stronger
344	than the seam's own second conjunct `HasRationalPoint C → IsIso …`.
345	
346	Given representability of `picSharp C`, the comparison
347	`PicScheme.picEtComparison C` is an isomorphism outright, with no section. So
348	under the campaign's endpoint the rational-point hypothesis of Kleiman §2
349	Thm 2.5 becomes redundant *for this curve*: it was buying a sheaf property that
350	representability already supplies.
351	
352	This is not a proof of Kleiman 2.5 — that theorem asserts the comparison is an
353	isomorphism from the section alone, with no representability input, and remains
354	unformalised. -/
355	theorem isIso_picEtComparison_of_picSharp_representability {k : Type u} [Field k]
356	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
357	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
358	    {X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))}
359	    (rep : (PicScheme.picSharp C).RepresentableBy X) :
360	    IsIso (PicScheme.picEtComparison C) :=
361	  PicScheme.isIso_picEtComparison_of_isSheaf C
362	    (PicScheme.relPresheaf_isSheaf_of_representableBy C rep)

364	/-! ## §4. The limit on the antecedent: representable implies *Zariski* sheaf
365	
366	The transport of §3 says the campaign needs no supplementary étale
367	representability theorem. This section says where the campaign may not put its
368	conclusion, and the two together are what actually price the board row.
369	
370	Attribution: this direction was pointed out by `review-ajc` on the §1–§3
371	commit, as a corollary of `relPresheaf_isSheaf_of_representableBy`. -/

373	namespace PicScheme
374	
375	/-- **A representable `picSharp` is a Zariski sheaf.**
376	
377	Immediate from subcanonicity of the *Zariski* topology on `(Sch/k)`
378	(`Scheme.subcanonical_zariskiTopology` through
379	`GrothendieckTopology.subcanonical_over`) — the étale route of §1 is not even
380	needed, though `zariskiTopologyOver_le_etaleTopologyOver` (`Picard/PicEtSheaf.lean`)
381	would also transport it from there.
382	
383	**What this rules out.** The seam docstring
384	(`Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean`, "Why sheafifying is what makes an
385	unconditional statement possible") argues *in prose* that an unconditional
386	`RepresentableBy` against `picSharp` is FALSE rather than unproved, because
387	some curve has a `picSharp` that is not a Zariski sheaf, while a representable
388	functor is a sheaf for any subcanonical topology.
389	
390	**That prose argument does not close, and this theorem is only its first half**
391	(`I-0970`). Its second half — a curve whose `picSharp` fails Zariski descent —
392	is not established by any source in the workspace: the seam's original citation
393	(§2 L1292–L1302) is about the *absolute* functor, its first replacement
394	(`ex:Pfs`) compares the two *sheafifications*, and `th:cmp` part 1 in fact gives
395	`picSharp ↪ Pic_{(X/S)zar}` on these binders. What IS established, and needs no
396	sheaf step, is Kleiman's own L5105–L5108: for the real conic `u²+v²+w²=0`
397	(smooth, proper, geometrically integral, no rational point) `Pic_{X/ℝ}` is not
398	representable while `Pic_{(X/ℝ)ét}` is. So the conclusion — over an arbitrary
399	field, no scheme represents `picSharp C` in general — stands on that quotation,
400	not on this theorem.
401	
402	The campaign milestones G3 and G4 conclude exactly that (G3: `J_r := J'_r/Γ`
403	represents `picSharpDeg C r` over `k`; G4 assembles `picSharpDeg`), so they are
404	targeting a false statement as written and need restating against `picEt`. That
405	restatement is the content of the board row `AJC.picrep.etale-rep`, and it is
406	what makes the row a *route repair* rather than a missing theorem.
407	
408	**The binder check, which the earlier text here left open, now closes**: the
409	witness is a smooth plane conic over `ℝ`, hence smooth, proper and
410	geometrically integral — this file's exact binders — and it has no `ℝ`-point,
411	which is what makes the two functors differ. So the antecedent of this theorem
412	is genuinely uninhabitable in general, not merely unproved.
413	
414	What remains unformalised is the *counterexample itself* (that `Pic_{X/ℝ}` of
415	that conic is not representable); it is quoted from Kleiman rather than
416	constructed in Lean. `not_representableBy_picSharp_of_not_isIso_picEtComparison`
417	below isolates exactly what a Lean version of it would have to supply. -/
418	theorem picSharp_isSheaf_zariski_of_representableBy {k : Type u} [Field k]
419	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
420	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
421	    {X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))}
422	    (rep : (picSharp C).RepresentableBy X) :
423	    Presieve.IsSheaf (Scheme.zariskiTopology.over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
424	      (picSharp C) := by
425	  haveI : (picSharp C).IsRepresentable := ⟨X, ⟨rep⟩⟩
426	  exact GrothendieckTopology.Subcanonical.isSheaf_of_isRepresentable _
427	
428	/-- **Kleiman's non-representability argument, as a Lean theorem: if the
429	comparison is not an isomorphism then `picSharp` is not representable.**
430	
431	This is the honest replacement for the Zariski-sheaf mechanism above, and it is
432	strictly better: it needs no sheaf step and no topology, only §3.
433	
434	Kleiman's own reasoning at L5105–L5108 and L5126–L5129 is exactly this. For the
435	real conic he shows `Pic_{X/ℝ}` and `Pic_{(X/ℝ)ét}` *differ*, and concludes
436	"`Pic_{X/ℝ}` is not representable" — with `Pic_{(X/ℝ)ét}` representable by the
437	Main Theorem. The inference from "they differ" to "the unsheafified one is not
438	representable" is not stated as needing an argument in the source; here it is
439	one, and it is the contrapositive of
440	`isIso_picEtComparison_of_picSharp_representability`: representability of
441	`picSharp` forces the comparison to be an isomorphism, so the two functors
442	cannot differ.
443	
444	**This is what converts the route claim from a quotation into a reduction.**
445	Combined with §3, the campaign's tail is constrained as follows: any proof that
446	some scheme represents `picSharp C` over a general field `k` would prove that
447	`picEtComparison C` is an isomorphism for every such `C` — including curves with
448	no `k`-point, where Kleiman exhibits it as non-surjective. So G3 and G4 cannot
449	be proved as written, and the repair is to descend `picEt`.
450	
451	**The one thing still quoted rather than proved**: that the comparison genuinely
452	fails to be an isomorphism for that conic. Formalising it means producing a
453	class in `picEt C (Spec ℝ)` outside the image — Kleiman's `φ*O(1)`, whose
454	argument runs through `h⁰` on `ℙ¹_ℂ` and flat base change. That is a bounded,
455	well-specified piece of work, and this theorem is the interface it would plug
456	into. -/
457	theorem not_representableBy_picSharp_of_not_isIso_picEtComparison {k : Type u} [Field k]
458	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
459	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
460	    (hne : ¬ IsIso (picEtComparison C)) (X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) :
461	    IsEmpty ((picSharp C).RepresentableBy X) :=
462	  ⟨fun rep => hne (Scheme.isIso_picEtComparison_of_picSharp_representability C rep)⟩
463	
464	/-- The same statement in the shape the seam's clause (1) uses: if the
465	comparison fails to be an isomorphism, the `picSharp` analogue of clause (1) is
466	FALSE — no scheme at all represents `picSharp C`, with or without the
467	finiteness and separatedness conjuncts.
468	
469	This is the precise sense in which the campaign's endpoint is not merely
470	unproved. Note the quantifier: `X` ranges over all `k`-schemes, so this refutes
471	the existential, not just the pinned witness `PicScheme C`. -/
472	theorem not_exists_representing_picSharp_of_not_isIso {k : Type u} [Field k]
473	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
474	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
475	    (hne : ¬ IsIso (picEtComparison C)) :
476	    ¬ ∃ X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)),
477	        Nonempty ((picSharp C).RepresentableBy X) ∧
478	          LocallyOfFiniteType X.hom ∧ IsSeparated X.hom := by
479	  rintro ⟨X, ⟨rep⟩, -, -⟩
480	  exact (not_representableBy_picSharp_of_not_isIso_picEtComparison C hne X).false rep
481	
482	end PicScheme
483	
484	end Scheme
485	
486	end AlgebraicGeometry

1	/-

6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.FGAPicRepresentability
7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.EtaleFieldCover
8	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.PicEtSubcanonical
9	
10	/-!
11	# Field 3 of the seam's clause (1): separatedness comes from the group structure
12	
13	`AJC.picrep.etale-rep.separated`.
14	
15	## What this file is for
16	
17	The seam `sorry` `Scheme.fgaPicardRepresentability`
18	(`Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean`) has as its clause (1) a **three-field**
19	existential:
20	
21	```
22	∃ X, Nonempty ((PicScheme.picEt C).RepresentableBy X) ∧
23	       LocallyOfFiniteType X.hom ∧ IsSeparated X.hom
24	```
25	
26	Every `AJC.picrep.etale-rep` row, and the seam's own four-input paragraph, price
27	the **first** field only (measured by `review-ajc`, `I-1286`: a grep for either
28	side conjunct across those rows returns zero hits). This file discharges the
29	**third** field outright, for an arbitrary smooth proper curve over an arbitrary
30	field, from nothing but a representation.
31	
32	## Why it is not a descent obligation, which is the reusable part
33	
34	The natural expectation is that separatedness travels across the field-extension
35	cover with the rest of the descent step. **It cannot**, with Mathlib `v4.31`, and
36	the lemma one would cite does not exist. Re-measured here independently of
37	`I-1286`, by `infer_instance` with the goal stated:
38	
39	* `MorphismProperty.DescendsAlong @IsSeparated (@Surjective ⊓ @Flat ⊓ @QuasiCompact)`
40	  — **fails** to synthesize;
41	* the diagonal route fails too, because
42	  `DescendsAlong @IsClosedImmersion (…)` is **also** absent (`IsClosedImmersion`
43	  is not a `HasRingHomProperty`, so `HasRingHomProperty.descendsAlong_flat` does
44	  not apply).
45	
46	So a lane arriving at the descent step intending to carry separatedness over has
47	nothing to carry it with. The route here bypasses the descent step entirely:
48	`picEt` is `CommGrpCat`-valued (`Scheme.picEtCommGrp`), so **any** scheme
49	representing it is a group object over `Spec k` by Yoneda transport, and a group
50	scheme over a field is separated. No cover, no descent, no field extension.
51	
52	Contrast field 2: `LocallyOfFiniteType` *does* descend freely at the real cover
53	— `Spec.map (algebraMap k k')` is `Surjective`, `Flat` and `QuasiCompact` by
54	synthesis for `k'/k` finite separable, and the `DescendsAlong` instance for
55	`LocallyOfFiniteType` exists. §4 carries that out
56	(`locallyOfFiniteType_of_baseChange`), so the contrast is compiler-checked rather
57	than asserted: **the two side conjuncts are free for opposite reasons**, and only
58	one of them is a descent argument. A costing that treats them as one item gets
59	one of them right for the wrong reason.
60	
61	## The brick, and where it came from
62	
63	"A group scheme over a field is separated" is **absent from Mathlib**: measured
64	both ways in one probe — `IsClosedImmersion η[G].left` synthesizes for
65	`[GrpObj G]` over `Spec K`, while `IsSeparated G.hom` **fails**. It is absent
66	from this project too (all three names below were new here). The sibling project
67	`Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild` has it at
68	`AbelianVariety/GroupSeparated.lean`; §1–§2 are that argument, and they compiled
69	here unchanged against this file's single import.
70	
71	Per `I-1287`: the ported statements were checked by elaborating them here, not by
72	reading the sibling's declaration headers — a `variable`-line binder is invisible
73	in a header. The sibling *file* is not Mathlib-only (its import chain runs through
74	`JacobianData`), so a header grep would misprice this as a cross-project
75	dependency; the two declarations used below need nothing from that chain, and the
76	evidence is that they elaborate here.
77	
78	## What this does NOT do
79	
80	It does not close the seam `sorry` and does not witness field 1 for any curve.
81	`k'`-side representability of `picEt` is still the campaign's undischarged
82	output, and §3's reduction takes it as a hypothesis. Nothing here is
83	`sorry`-reachable: all seven declarations report
84	`[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]` against
85	`Scheme.fgaPicardRepresentability` as a control that reports `sorryAx`, per
86	`I-1251` — on this seam the axiom list discriminates and provability does not,
87	because `instHasPicSchemeEt` is unconditional.
88	
89	**Non-vacuity, measured rather than asserted.** Dropping `rep` from §2 leaves
90	`IsSeparated X.hom` for an arbitrary `X`, and `infer_instance` **fails** — so the
91	representation is load-bearing, not decoration. And `LocallyOfFiniteType X.hom`
92	does **not** follow from `rep` (`exact?` fails), so §3 is not quietly absorbing
93	field 2: it is stated as a hypothesis because it is one.
94	-/
95	
96	universe v₁ u₁ u
97	
98	open CategoryTheory AlgebraicGeometry Limits MonoidalCategory
99	open CartesianMonoidalCategory MonObj
100	
101	namespace CategoryTheory
102	
103	/-! ## §1. The categorical half: the diagonal of a group object -/
104	
105	variable {D : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁} D] [CartesianMonoidalCategory D]
106	
107	/-- **The diagonal of a group object is the pullback of the unit along the
108	difference map** (Kleiman `lem:agps`(1), categorical half).
109	
110	For a group object `G` in any cartesian monoidal category, the square with top
111	`Δ = lift (𝟙 G) (𝟙 G)`, left `toUnit G`, right the difference map
112	`fst ⋅ snd⁻¹ : G ⊗ G ⟶ G` and bottom the unit `η[G]` is a pullback. Here `⋅`/`⁻¹`
113	are the Hom-group operations (scoped in `CategoryTheory.MonObj`), so the
114	difference map is `lift (fst G G) (snd G G ≫ ι) ≫ μ` definitionally.
115	
116	No geometry: the Hom-group calculus of `Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Monoidal/Cartesian`
117	does the work. Transcribed from the sibling project (see the module docstring). -/
118	theorem GrpObj.isPullback_diagonal (G : D) [GrpObj G] :
119	    IsPullback (toUnit G) (lift (𝟙 G) (𝟙 G)) η[G] (fst G G * (snd G G)⁻¹) where
120	  w := by
121	    rw [MonObj.comp_mul, GrpObj.comp_inv, lift_fst, lift_snd, mul_inv_cancel, Hom.one_def]
122	  isLimit' := Nonempty.intro <| PullbackCone.IsLimit.mk _
123	    (fun s => s.snd ≫ fst G G)
124	    (fun s => toUnit_unique _ _)
125	    (fun s => by
126	      -- the cone condition says `(s.snd ≫ fst) ⋅ (s.snd ≫ snd)⁻¹ = 1` in the Hom-group
127	      have key : s.snd ≫ fst G G = s.snd ≫ snd G G := by
128	        have h := s.condition.symm
129	        rw [MonObj.comp_mul, GrpObj.comp_inv, toUnit_unique s.fst (toUnit _),
130	          ← Hom.one_def] at h
131	        exact mul_inv_eq_one.mp h
132	      exact CartesianMonoidalCategory.hom_ext _ _ (by simp) (by simpa using key))
133	    (fun s m hm₁ hm₂ => by
134	      have := hm₂ =≫ fst G G
135	      simpa using this)
136	
137	end CategoryTheory
138	
139	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
140	
141	/-! ## §2. Group schemes are separated -/
142	
143	/-- **A group scheme whose unit section is a closed immersion is separated**
144	(Kleiman `lem:agps`(1)), over an arbitrary base scheme `S`.
145	
146	The diagonal is the base change of `η[G].left` along the difference map — §1
147	pushed to schemes by `Over.forget` — and closed immersions are stable under base
148	change. **No finiteness hypothesis**: `LocallyOfFiniteType` is not needed, which
149	matters here because field 2 of the seam's clause (1) is exactly the finiteness
150	conjunct and this must not consume it. -/
151	theorem isSeparated_of_isClosedImmersion_one {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : Over S) [GrpObj G]
152	    [IsClosedImmersion η[G].left] : IsSeparated G.hom := by
153	  constructor
154	  have sq := (GrpObj.isPullback_diagonal G).map (Over.forget S)
155	  exact MorphismProperty.of_isPullback sq ‹IsClosedImmersion η[G].left›
156	
157	/-- **A group scheme over a field is separated** (Kleiman `lem:agps`(1)).
158	
159	Over a field the closed-immersion hypothesis of
160	`isSeparated_of_isClosedImmersion_one` is Mathlib's own instance
161	(`AlgebraicGeometry/Group/Abelian.lean`). Absent from Mathlib as a whole,
162	though — measured both ways in one probe: `IsClosedImmersion η[G].left`
163	synthesizes here while `IsSeparated G.hom` does not, which is why this
164	`instance` is worth stating. -/
165	instance isSeparated_of_grpObj {K : Type u} [Field K] (G : Over (Spec (.of K)))
166	    [GrpObj G] : IsSeparated G.hom :=
167	  isSeparated_of_isClosedImmersion_one G
168	
169	/-! ## §3. Field 3 of the seam's clause (1) -/
170	
171	/-- **Any scheme representing `Pic_{(C/k)ét}` is separated over `k`** — field 3
172	of clause (1) of `Scheme.fgaPicardRepresentability`, discharged.
173	
174	Smooth proper curve over an **arbitrary** field, no hypothesis on `C(k)`
175	(`I-0491`), and no hypothesis on `X` beyond carrying the representation.
176	`picEt` is `CommGrpCat`-valued, so `CommGrpObj.ofRepresentableBy` transports the
177	group structure of the étale Picard sheaf onto `X` by Yoneda, and §2 applies.
178	
179	**The representation is load-bearing.** Dropping `rep` leaves `IsSeparated X.hom`
180	for an arbitrary `X` over `Spec k`, and `infer_instance` fails — so this is not a
181	statement that would have held anyway.
182	
183	`[SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom]` and `[IsProper C.hom]` are the binders of
184	`picEt`/`picEtCommGrp` themselves, needed to *name* the functor rather than by
185	the argument. `[GeometricallyIntegral C.hom]` — which the seam carries — is
186	**not** needed and is deliberately absent. -/
187	theorem isSeparated_of_representableBy_picEt {k : Type u} [Field k]
188	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
189	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
190	    {X : Over (Spec (.of k))} (rep : (Scheme.PicScheme.picEt C).RepresentableBy X) :
191	    IsSeparated X.hom :=
192	  letI : CommGrpObj X :=
193	    CommGrpObj.ofRepresentableBy X (Scheme.picEtCommGrp C)
194	      (rep.ofIso (Scheme.picEtCommGrpForgetIso C))
195	  isSeparated_of_grpObj X
196	
197	/-- **Clause (1) of the seam is a TWO-field obligation**: a representing scheme
198	that is locally of finite type suffices, and separatedness comes for free.
199	
200	This is the form a lane closing the descent step should aim at. It removes an
201	obligation that was never on any board row, and it forecloses the dead end: do
202	**not** budget a separatedness-descent argument, because (module docstring) the
203	`DescendsAlong` instance it would cite does not exist in Mathlib `v4.31`.
204	
205	**Not a discount on the seam.** The hypothesis is still the campaign's
206	undischarged output — a `k`-scheme representing `picEt C` — and this theorem
207	supplies no witness for it at any curve. What it changes is the *shape* of what
208	must be produced: two fields, not three. Field 2 stays a genuine obligation and
209	is not absorbed here: `LocallyOfFiniteType X.hom` does not follow from the
210	representation (`exact?` fails), which is why it is a hypothesis. At the real
211	cover it *does* descend freely, unlike field 3 — the two are free for opposite
212	reasons. -/
213	theorem seamClauseOne_of_representableBy_locallyOfFiniteType {k : Type u} [Field k]
214	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
215	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
216	    (h : ∃ X : Over (Spec (.of k)),
217	      Nonempty ((Scheme.PicScheme.picEt C).RepresentableBy X) ∧
218	        LocallyOfFiniteType X.hom) :
219	    ∃ X : Over (Spec (.of k)),
220	      Nonempty ((Scheme.PicScheme.picEt C).RepresentableBy X) ∧
221	        LocallyOfFiniteType X.hom ∧ IsSeparated X.hom := by
222	  obtain ⟨X, ⟨rep⟩, hlft⟩ := h
223	  exact ⟨X, ⟨rep⟩, hlft, isSeparated_of_representableBy_picEt C rep⟩
224	
225	/-- **The campaign's own endpoint drops to two fields as well.**
226	
227	`Scheme.hasPicSchemeEt_of_picSharp_representability`
228	(`Picard/PicEtSubcanonical.lean`) is the theorem that turns the Milne–Kollár
229	campaign's `picSharp`-shaped output into clause (1), and its hypothesis is a
230	*three*-field `picSharp` existential. The separatedness field is free there too,
231	and for the same reason: the transport
232	`Scheme.picSharp_representableBy_picEt_transport` does not move the representing
233	scheme, so the `picEt` representation lands on the **same** `X`, and §3 applies to
234	it.
235	
236	This is the form to hand the campaign: it must deliver a `picSharp`-representing
237	scheme that is locally of finite type, and **nothing about separatedness**.
238	
239	**Still not a discount on the seam.** The hypothesis is exactly what the campaign
240	has not delivered, and over an arbitrary `k` it is not merely unproved — there is
241	a refutation route mapped out for it
242	(`Scheme.PicScheme.not_exists_representing_picSharp_of_not_isIso`, conditional on
243	a comparison failure this project quotes rather than proves). What changes is only
244	how many fields the deliverable has. -/
245	theorem picEtClauseOne_of_picSharp_representableBy_locallyOfFiniteType
246	    {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
247	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
248	    (h : ∃ X : Over (Spec (.of k)),
249	      Nonempty ((Scheme.PicScheme.picSharp C).RepresentableBy X) ∧
250	        LocallyOfFiniteType X.hom) :
251	    ∃ X : Over (Spec (.of k)),
252	      Nonempty ((Scheme.PicScheme.picEt C).RepresentableBy X) ∧
253	        LocallyOfFiniteType X.hom ∧ IsSeparated X.hom := by
254	  obtain ⟨X, ⟨rep⟩, hlft⟩ := h
255	  have repEt := Scheme.picSharp_representableBy_picEt_transport C rep
256	  exact ⟨X, ⟨repEt⟩, hlft, isSeparated_of_representableBy_picEt C repEt⟩
257	
258	/-! ## §4. Field 2, for contrast: it DOES descend, at the route's own cover -/
259	
260	/-- **Field 2 descends along the field-extension cover.** If the base change of
261	`X` to `k'` is locally of finite type over `Spec k'`, then `X` is locally of
262	finite type over `Spec k`, for `k'/k` finite separable.
263	
264	Recorded here, beside field 3, because the *contrast* is the planning fact: field
265	2 is free by a **descent** argument (Mathlib has
266	`DescendsAlong @LocallyOfFiniteType (@Surjective ⊓ @Flat ⊓ @QuasiCompact)`, and
267	`Spec.map (algebraMap k k')` satisfies all three by synthesis — surjectivity from
268	`Scheme.surjective_specMap_algebraMap`, the other two outright), while field 3 is
269	free *only* because descent is unavailable for it and the group structure
270	substitutes. A lane that priced the two conjuncts together would get one of them
271	right for the wrong reason.
272	
273	Nothing about `picEt` occurs: this is a statement about an arbitrary `k`-scheme,
274	and it is stated at that generality on purpose so that no reader takes it for a
275	fact about the Picard functor. -/
276	theorem locallyOfFiniteType_of_baseChange {k : Type u} [Field k] (k' : Type u)
277	    [Field k'] [Algebra k k'] [Algebra.IsSeparable k k'] [Module.Finite k k']
278	    {X : Over (Spec (.of k))}
279	    (h : LocallyOfFiniteType
280	      (Limits.pullback.fst (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k k'))) X.hom)) :
281	    LocallyOfFiniteType X.hom := by
282	  have hQ : (@Surjective ⊓ @Flat ⊓ @QuasiCompact : MorphismProperty Scheme)
283	      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k k'))) :=
284	    ⟨⟨Scheme.surjective_specMap_algebraMap k k', inferInstance⟩, inferInstance⟩
285	  exact MorphismProperty.of_pullback_fst_of_descendsAlong hQ h
286	
287	end AlgebraicGeometry
288

110	  legacy `picSharp`-shaped interface, whose only producer is now the
111	  conditional `picSchemeOfHasRationalPoint`. Consumers quantifying over
112	  `[HasPicScheme C]` as a hypothesis remain valid and kernel-clean; they are
113	  simply conditional statements until restated against `picEt`.
114	
115	## Main results
116	
117	* `fgaPicardRepresentability` — **the project's central open obligation**:
118	  representability of `Pic_{(C/k)ét}` over an arbitrary field, no rational
119	  point. The file's only `sorry`.
120	* `HasPicSchemeEt`, `PicSchemeEt`, `representableEt`,
121	  `instPicSchemeEtLocallyOfFiniteType`, `instPicSchemeEtIsSeparated`,
122	  `groupSchemeStructureEt` — the unconditional étale interface derived from it.
123	* `picEtComparison_isIso_of_hasRationalPoint`, `picSchemeOfHasRationalPoint` —
124	  the **conditional** Kleiman §2 Thm 2.5 route, strictly weaker than the
125	  challenge, not the headline.
126	* `picSharp` — the relative Picard functor `Pic^♯_{C/k}`.
127	* `divFunctor` — the relative-divisor functor `Scheme.DivFunctor C.hom` of
128	  `Picard/DivFunctorDef.lean` (Kleiman §3 Def. `df:div`, invertible-kernel
129	  quotient encoding).
130	* `PicScheme`, `representable`, `instPicSharpRepresentable` — the representing
131	  scheme and the natural bijection
132	  `(T ⟶ Pic_{C/k}) ≃ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)` it induces.
133	* `instPicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType`, `isSeparated` — `Pic_{C/k}` is locally
134	  of finite type and separated over `k` (Kleiman §4 Thm `th:main`(1): it is a
135	  disjoint union of open quasi-projective `k`-subschemes).
136	* `groupSchemeStructure` — `Pic_{C/k}` is a commutative `k`-group scheme, by
137	  Yoneda transport (`CommGrpObj.ofRepresentableBy`) of the abelian-group
138	  structure of `PicSharp.relPresheaf`.
139	* `abelMapWitness`, `abelMap`, `abelMap_app_mk` — the Abel map
140	  `Div_{C/k} ⟶ Pic^♯_{C/k}`, `[D] ↦ [O(D)] = -[ker q]` (Kleiman §3
141	  Def. `dfn:Abel`), assembled as `abelKernelNatTrans C ≫ picNeg C`.
142	* `smoothProperQuotient` — the Altman–Kleiman quotient lemma (Kleiman §4
143	  Lem. `lm:qt`), relative to the use-site hypothesis class
144	  `HasSmoothProperQuotient`.
145	
146	## Remaining obligations
147	
148	**Exactly one** statement in this file is `sorry`: `fgaPicardRepresentability`,
149	the existence of a scheme representing the étale-sheafified relative Picard
150	functor `Pic_{(C/k)ét}` and separated and locally of finite type over `k`, for
151	an arbitrary field `k` and **no** hypothesis on `C(k)`. Mathematically this is
152	Kleiman §4 Thm `th:main`(1) together with Cor `cor:algsch`. It is the project's
153	central open obligation and is **expected to stay open**. Its inputs are the
154	Milne–Kollár ones — `Div^d` through the Grassmannian and a finite Galois
155	quotient — *not* Quot and *not* `smoothProperQuotient`; see the "Which route
156	discharges it" paragraph on `fgaPicardRepresentability` below, which corrects an
157	earlier claim here that the inputs were blocked on Quot. Everything else here —
158	the representing scheme,
159	its representability, local finiteness, separatedness and group-scheme
160	structure, and the conditional `picSchemeOfHasRationalPoint` — is derived from
161	that one existence statement.
162	
163	`smoothProperQuotient` is stated against an explicit hypothesis class rather
164	than proved outright, because the hypothesis list expressible here is weaker

226	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicSchemeEt C] :
227	    UniversallyClosed (Pic0SchemeEt C).hom :=
228	  sorry
229	
230	/-- **`Pic⁰_{C/k}` is proper over `k`** — assembly of the two proved conjuncts
231	with the single open one. -/
232	theorem proper {k : Type u} [Field k]
233	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
234	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
235	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicSchemeEt C] :
236	    IsProper (Pic0SchemeEt C).hom := by
237	  haveI : IsSeparated (Pic0SchemeEt C).hom := isSeparated C
238	  haveI : LocallyOfFiniteType (Pic0SchemeEt C).hom := locallyOfFiniteType C
239	  haveI := universallyClosed C
240	  constructor
241	
242	end Pic0Et
243	
244	end Scheme

246	end AlgebraicGeometry
