6	import Mathlib
7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.PicEtCrossBase
8	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.EtaleFieldCover
9	
10	/-!
11	# The descent assembly — the theorem that CONSUMES the four repair inputs
12	
13	`AJC.picrep.etale-rep.descent-assembly`.
14	
15	## Why this file exists
16	
17	The repaired route to the seam `sorry` `Scheme.fgaPicardRepresentability`
18	(`Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean`) is documented at that declaration as
19	having **four inputs**, and each of the four has either landed or is held by a
20	lane. What no declaration in this project stated is the theorem those four are
21	inputs *to*: the step that takes a representation over a larger field and
22	returns one over `k`.
23	
24	Measured before this file was written, at HEAD with fresh oleans: the seam's
25	conclusion shape `Nonempty ((PicScheme.picEt C).RepresentableBy X)` occurs at
26	exactly three sites — `Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean` twice (the
27	`HasPicSchemeEt` class field, and the `sorry`-bodied seam itself) and
28	`Picard/PicEtSubcanonical.lean` once
29	(`hasPicSchemeEt_of_picSharp_representability`). All three are **same-field**:
30	the last takes a `picSharp` representation over the *same* `k` and transports it
31	along subcanonicity. None takes a `k'`-side representation and concludes over
32	`k`. Independently re-measured by `review-ajc` (`I-1256`) before this file
33	landed.
34	
35	So the route's scoreboard was a list of antecedents with no goal attached, and an
36	input nobody held would have stayed invisible — the failure mode this file is
37	written to remove.
38	
39	## What is proved here, and what is not
40	
41	**Proved, `sorry`-free** (§2): the **uniqueness half** of the descent, at the
42	cover the repair uses. `picEt_injective_restrict_baseTest` says restriction along
43	the single morphism `T ×_k k' ⟶ T` is *injective* on `picEt`-classes, for every
44	`k`-test `T`. This is what makes a descended class unique once it exists.
45	
46	**Proved, `sorry`-free** (§3): the transport that makes the `k'`-side hypothesis
47	statable in the right variables (`representableByRestrict_of_baseChange`, free from
48	input 2). The other half of the class-level descent — a compatible family has a
49	unique amalgamation — is `Scheme.isSheafFor_picEt_pullback_presieve`
50	(`Picard/EtaleFieldCover.lean`), cited in §3 rather than restated.
51	
52	**Not proved, and named rather than hidden** (§4): `G1` invariance — producing the
53	compatible family from a Galois-invariant `k'`-class — and then the `G2` quotient
54	construction that turns descended classes into a representing `k`-scheme, gated on
55	`AlgebraicJacobian.GaloisDescent.HasGaloisQuotient` (affine half only). Neither is
56	sheaf-theoretic; this file does not weaken either, does not restate them more
57	cheaply, and does not close them.
58	
59	**What this file deliberately does not contain.** An earlier draft stated the
60	assembly as a Lean implication whose antecedent was the seam's clause (1) and whose
61	conclusion was the same existential — i.e. `P → P`, the shape `I-0838` forbids and
62	the 2026-07-29 audit found 67 times. It was removed before committing rather than
63	dressed up: the remaining obligation is a *construction*, so its home is the gate
64	in `Picard/FiniteGaloisQuotient.lean`, not a hypothesis slot here. Nor is any
65	conclusion in this file class-valued: because `instHasPicSchemeEt` is
66	unconditional, instance search discharges a `HasPicSchemeEt`-valued conclusion by
67	projecting the seam `sorry` for every object in the gate's domain, so such a
68	statement would typecheck whatever its hypotheses said (`review-ajc`, `I-1251`).
69	
70	## What this does NOT do
71	
72	It closes no `sorry` in `Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean` and witnesses no
73	antecedent of `fgaPicardRepresentability` for any curve. §2 is a genuine theorem
74	about `picEt` on an arbitrary smooth proper curve over an arbitrary field, with no
75	hypothesis on `C(k)` per `I-0491`; the statements of §3 are unconditional, and what
76	§4 records as remaining has no producer.
77	
78	## A route correction recorded here because it was nearly acted on
79	
80	`review-ajc` proposed (and, once shown this, withdrew — `I-1256`) that the
81	assembly should conclude the `picSharp`-shaped endpoint
82	`∃ X, Nonempty ((picSharp C).RepresentableBy X) ∧ LocallyOfFiniteType X.hom ∧
83	IsSeparated X.hom`, on the strength of its own r5 measurement that this single
84	existential discharges *both* seam conjuncts with nothing left over. That
85	reduction is correct and is cited below at the **input** end. As a *conclusion*
86	over the headline's arbitrary `k` it is inadmissible, and this project already
87	proves why: `PicScheme.not_exists_representing_picSharp_of_not_isIso`
88	(`Picard/PicEtSubcanonical.lean`) says no scheme at all represents `picSharp C`
89	over such a `k` once `picEtComparison C` fails to be an isomorphism. Aiming the
90	assembly there would have produced a green, `sorry`-free theorem refutable from a
91	lemma two files away. The whole content of the repair is that the object crossing
92	the descent step is `picEt`.
93	
94	## Measurement discipline
95	
96	`lake build AlgebraicJacobian` EXIT=0 (8869 jobs) with **fresh** oleans before
97	every probe below — a stale-import environment reports every probe as succeeding
98	(`I-1057`), which would have made the §2 proof look free when it was not.
99	-/
100	
101	universe u
102	
103	open CategoryTheory AlgebraicGeometry Limits
104	
105	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
106	
107	namespace Scheme
108	
109	namespace PicScheme
110	
111	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {k' : Type u} [Field k'] [Algebra k k']
112	
113	/-! ## §1. The cover of a `k`-test by its base change, as an `Over`-morphism -/
114	
115	/-- The base change `T ×_k Spec k'` of a `k`-test `T`, regarded as a `k'`-test
116	via the second projection.
117	
118	This is the object the descent step's classes live on: a class over `k'` is a
119	class on `T_{k'}` for the tests `T` of interest, and `§2` shows a `k`-class is
120	determined by its restriction here. -/
121	noncomputable abbrev baseTest (T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) :
122	    Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k')) :=
123	  Over.mk (pullback.snd T.hom (specMapAlgebra k k'))
124	
125	/-- **The covering morphism `T_{k'} ⟶ T`**, in the slice over `Spec k`.
126	
127	Its underlying scheme map is exactly `pullback.fst`, which is the morphism
128	`Picard/EtaleFieldCover.lean` builds its covering sieve from — so the sheaf
129	axiom landed there applies to this morphism on the nose (checked by `rfl`:
130	`coverMap_left`). -/
131	noncomputable def coverMap (T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) :
132	    (restrictTest k k').obj (baseTest (k' := k') T) ⟶ T :=
133	  Over.homMk (pullback.fst T.hom (specMapAlgebra k k'))
134	    (pullback.condition (f := T.hom) (g := specMapAlgebra k k'))
135	
136	/-- The cover morphism's underlying scheme map **is** `pullback.fst`, definitionally.
137	
138	This is the identification that lets `§2` feed
139	`Scheme.picEt_ext_of_pullback_agrees`, whose sieve is generated by
140	`Presieve.singleton (pullback.fst T.hom (specMapAlgebra k k'))`. -/
141	@[simp]
142	theorem coverMap_left (T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) :
143	    (coverMap (k' := k') T).left = pullback.fst T.hom (specMapAlgebra k k') := rfl
144	
145	/-! ## §2. The uniqueness half of the descent — PROVED -/
146	
147	/-- **Restriction along `T_{k'} ⟶ T` is injective on `picEt`-classes.**
148	
149	For a smooth proper curve `C` over an arbitrary field `k`, an arbitrary finite
150	separable `k'/k`, and an arbitrary `k`-test `T`: two classes in
151	`Pic_{(C/k)ét}(T)` that agree after restriction to `T ×_k Spec k'` are equal.
152	
153	This is the *uniqueness* half of the descent step, and it is what makes a
154	descended class unique once one exists — so a consumer holding a single class,
155	rather than a compatible family, needs no separate uniqueness hypothesis.
156	
157	**Where the content is, stated precisely.** The amalgamation property itself is
158	free: `Scheme.isSheafFor_picEt_of_mem` holds at *every* covering sieve of
159	`etaleTopologyOver k`, `⊤` included, because it is `PicSharp.etaleSheaf`'s own
160	`Sheaf.cond` pushed through the forgetful functor. What this lemma adds over
161	`Scheme.picEt_ext_of_pullback_agrees` is the reduction from that lemma's
162	*sieve-indexed* hypothesis — agreement after restriction along **every** arrow of
163	the generated sieve — to agreement along the **single** morphism `coverMap`. The
164	step is the factorisation: an arrow of the sieve factors through `pullback.fst`,
165	and lifting that factorisation to the slice over `Spec k` is where
166	`pullback.condition` is consumed.
167	
168	**That the factorisation is not avoidable is measured, not assumed** — it is the
169	obvious refutation of this lemma ("the sheaf axiom gives injectivity directly, so
170	the hand proof is redundant"), so it was probed rather than argued. Two routes,
171	both `EXIT=1`:
172	
173	* deriving it from the amalgamation statement
174	  (`Scheme.isSheafFor_picEt_pullback_presieve`) requires exhibiting a
175	  `Presieve.FamilyOfElements` on the *whole* sieve for which both classes are
176	  amalgamations, and constructing that family needs a value at every sieve arrow —
177	  i.e. the same factorisation, relocated;
178	* discharging the sieve-indexed goal from the single-morphism hypothesis with no
179	  factorisation work fails: `exact h`, `simpa using h`, `congrArg _ h` and `aesop`
180	  all leave the goal open (`aesop` reports exhaustive search).
181	
182	So the content is the reduction, and only the reduction. Whoever re-checks this
183	should re-run those two probes rather than trust the paragraph.
184	
185	**No hypothesis on `C(k)`** (`I-0491`), and none on `T`. The finite-separability
186	binders are inherited from the covering-sieve membership witness of
187	`Picard/EtaleFieldCover.lean`, which is where they are genuinely used; they are
188	*not* needed by the cross-base identification (`picEt_crossBaseIso` holds for an
189	arbitrary field extension). -/
190	theorem picEt_injective_restrict_baseTest
191	    [FiniteDimensional k k'] [Algebra.IsSeparable k k']
192	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
193	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
194	    (T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
195	    {t₁ t₂ : (picEt C).obj (Opposite.op T)}
196	    (h : (picEt C).map (coverMap (k' := k') T).op t₁
197	       = (picEt C).map (coverMap (k' := k') T).op t₂) :
198	    t₁ = t₂ := by
199	  refine AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.picEt_ext_of_pullback_agrees k' C T ?_
200	  intro W g hg
201	  rw [Sieve.overEquiv_symm_iff] at hg
202	  obtain ⟨Z, a, b, hb, hfac⟩ := hg
203	  cases hb
204	  -- `g` factors through `coverMap` in the slice over `Spec k`.
205	  have hgfac : g = (Over.homMk a (by
206	      rw [← Over.w g]
207	      simp only [restrictTest, Over.map_obj_hom, baseTest, Over.mk_hom, ← hfac]
208	      rw [Category.assoc]
209	      exact congrArg (a ≫ ·) pullback.condition.symm) :
210	        W ⟶ (restrictTest k k').obj (baseTest (k' := k') T))
211	      ≫ coverMap (k' := k') T := by
212	    apply Over.OverMorphism.ext
213	    change Over.Hom.left g = a ≫ pullback.fst T.hom (specMapAlgebra k k')
214	    exact hfac.symm
215	  rw [hgfac]
216	  simp only [op_comp, Functor.map_comp, CategoryTheory.comp_apply, h]
217	
218	/-! ## §3. The input-side transport, and the sharp form of what remains -/
219	
220	/-- **The `k'`-side input, transported: PROVED, and free.**
221	
222	A representation of `picEt` of the **base-changed curve** `C_{k'}` by a
223	`k'`-scheme `X'` is the same thing as a representation of `picEt C` restricted to
224	`k'`-tests. This is `picEt_crossBaseIso` (input 2 of the repair, closed
225	unconditionally by `Picard/PicEtCrossBase.lean`) fed to
226	`Functor.RepresentableBy.ofIso`.
227	
228	It is recorded because it is the step that makes the assembly's hypothesis
229	*statable in the right variables*: without it the `k'`-scheme that campaign `J5`
230	produces would represent `picEt` of the `k`-curve restricted to `k'`-tests rather
231	than `picEt` of `C_{k'}`, and there would be no functor for the Galois action to
232	act on — a mismatch no green build reveals.
233	
234	No separability or finiteness hypothesis on `k'/k`: the cross-base identification
235	never needed one. -/
236	noncomputable def representableByRestrict_of_baseChange
237	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
238	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
239	    {X' : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k'))}
240	    (rep : (picEt (Scheme.baseChangeField C k')).RepresentableBy X') :
241	    ((restrictTest k k').op ⋙ picEt C).RepresentableBy X' :=
242	  rep.ofIso (picEt_crossBaseIso C k')
243	
244	/-! ### The other half — free, and already in the tree
245	
246	A *compatible family* of `picEt C`-classes on this cover has a **unique**
247	amalgamation, so descent of classes along the cover is settled outright and nothing
248	about it is owed. That is
249	`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.isSheafFor_picEt_pullback_presieve`
250	(`Picard/EtaleFieldCover.lean`), and it is cited rather than restated here.
251	
252	**An earlier revision of this file restated it** as an
253	`existsUnique_amalgamation_picEt_fieldCover`, describing the restatement's value as
254	"the pricing consequence". A fresh-context audit measured the two `rfl`-equal —
255	*proposition and term* — and pointed at `EtaleFieldCover.lean`'s own `:289`/`:294`,
256	which already say "unique amalgamation" and "every covering sieve, `⊤` included,
257	free from sheafification" (`I-1312`). So the pricing fact was in the tree as prose
258	and the declaration added nothing; it is deleted rather than kept with a caveat, per
259	`I-1284`. The same audit deleted a second self-downgraded lemma from this file.
260	
261	**The pricing fact itself stands**, and it is what a lane needs: the residue of the
262	descent step is **not** in the sheaf theory. It is in two places this file does not
263	reach —
264	
265	1. producing the *compatible family* from a Galois-**invariant** `k'`-class, the
266	   Hilbert-90/invariance content of campaign `G1`, where the group action enters; and
267	2. the **scheme-level** quotient — turning descended classes into a `k`-scheme
268	   representing `picEt C` — campaign `G2`, gated on
269	   `AlgebraicJacobian.GaloisDescent.HasGaloisQuotient`.
270	
271	Budget those two and *nothing* for the sheaf-theoretic halves.
272	-/
273	
274	
275	/-! ## §4. What still stands between this and the seam's clause (1)
276	
277	The seam's clause (1) asks for a `k`-scheme representing `picEt C`. What `§3`
278	establishes is that the *class-level* descent along the field-extension cover is
279	**complete**: a compatible family has a unique amalgamation, both halves free from
280	sheafification once the covering-sieve witness of `Picard/EtaleFieldCover.lean` is
281	in hand. What this file does **not** supply, and therefore leaves open, is two
282	things, neither of them sheaf-theoretic:
283	
284	* producing the compatible family from a Galois-invariant `k'`-class (the
285	  invariance content of campaign `G1`); and
286	* the passage from descended classes to a *representing scheme* over `k` — the
287	  quotient construction itself (campaign `G2`), which produces the `k`-scheme as a
288	  quotient of `X'` by the semilinear Galois action, gated on
289	  `AlgebraicJacobian.GaloisDescent.HasGaloisQuotient`. That gate now has a global
290	  instance on the **affine** locus (`Picard/GaloisQuotientAffineGeneral.lean`,
291	  `ajc-p1`), while the object this route descends is glued, so it still bites.
292	
293	Deliberately **not** stated here as a Lean implication with that passage as a
294	hypothesis: an implication whose antecedent is its own conclusion is `P → P`, and
295	an implication whose antecedent is "the `k`-scheme exists with its properties" is
296	that. The route's remaining obligation is a *construction*, and the place for it is
297	`Picard/FiniteGaloisQuotient.lean`'s gate, where it already sits.
298	
299	And clause (1) is a **one-conjunct** obligation, not three — measured by
300	`review-ajc` (`I-1286`) after this file's first revision, which priced only the
301	representability field and said nothing about the other two. Both side conjuncts
302	are free: `LocallyOfFiniteType` descends along exactly this cover (it is one of the
303	five scheme flat-descent instances mathlib has), and `IsSeparated` never needs to
304	descend at all — `picEt` is group-valued, so any representing scheme is a group
305	object by Yoneda transport and a group scheme over a field is separated. Note the
306	direction: `IsSeparated` *cannot* descend in mathlib v4.31 (no `DescendsAlong`
307	instance, and the diagonal route needs one for `IsClosedImmersion`, also absent),
308	so the free route is the only route. The one brick is a port of AJCR's
309	`AbelianVariety/GroupSeparated.lean`.
310	
311	So the scoreboard this file was written to complete reads, at HEAD: inputs 1 (the
312	cover), 2 (cross-base), 4 (the `k^s` section) landed; input 3 (the Galois quotient)
313	open, gated, affine half only; the *goal* they feed now exists, with its
314	class-level half **closed**; and of the goal's three conjuncts only
315	representability is owed. The remaining cost is `G1` invariance and the `G2`
316	quotient — and `k'`-side representability itself, which is the campaign's
317	undischarged output and is not made cheaper by any of this.
318	-/
319	
320	end PicScheme
321	
322	end Scheme
323	
324	end AlgebraicGeometry

465	**How many inputs the repair has, and which are now in hand** — the count has
466	moved twice, so it is stated here as a history rather than as a fact.
467	"Descend `picEt` instead of `picSharp`" was priced at two inputs (2026-07-29
468	`ajc-p1`), then three (`review-ajc`, adding the cross-base identification), and
469	is now **four** (`review-ajc`, `I-1135`, adding the section over separably closed
470	fields that everything else silently assumes) — **plus a fifth entry added
471	2026-07-30 which is a subtraction, not an input**: all four price the
472	`RepresentableBy` field of clause (1), and the *other two fields of that same
473	clause* are free (item 5 below, `I-1286`).
474	
475	**And a list of inputs is not a route — corrected 2026-07-30 (`ajc-p2`), because
476	for four rounds this paragraph was one.** Every entry below is an *antecedent*.
477	There is **still** no declaration anywhere in this project stating the theorem they
478	are antecedents *of*, and an earlier revision of this paragraph — written by the
479	lane that added `Picard/PicEtDescentAssembly.lean` — claimed that file supplied
480	one. **It does not** (refuted by a fresh-context audit, `I-1312`, reproduced and
481	accepted by its author): none of that file's declarations takes a `k'`-side
482	representation and concludes over `k`. Its
483	`representableByRestrict_of_baseChange` concludes a `RepresentableBy` for a
484	`k'`-**object**, i.e. it restates the `k'`-side input in the right variables rather
485	than crossing the descent step. The census below is accurate; the remedy is not
486	applied. The conclusion shape
487	`Nonempty ((PicScheme.picEt C).RepresentableBy X)` occurred at exactly three sites
488	— the `HasPicSchemeEt` class field and the seam `sorry` below, plus
489	`hasPicSchemeEt_of_picSharp_representability` — and all three are **same-field**,
490	none taking a representation over a larger field and concluding over `k`
491	(measured by `ajc-p2`, re-measured independently by `review-ajc`, `I-1256`). With
492	the goal unwritten, an input nobody held would not have shown up as missing.
493	
494	What *is* settled, and it is a pricing fact rather than a step: do **not** budget
495	effectivity of `picEt`-**classes** along the field-extension cover. Both halves are
496	free from sheafification — `Picard/EtaleFieldCover.lean` already says so in prose at
497	its own §4 (`:289`, `:294`: "unique amalgamation", "every covering sieve, `⊤`
498	included, free from sheafification"), and `PicEtDescentAssembly.lean`'s
499	`existsUnique_amalgamation_picEt_fieldCover` is that lemma `rfl`-equal, proposition
500	and term (`I-1312`). Its `picEt_injective_restrict_baseTest` is the
501	sieve-to-single-morphism reduction; that step is unavoidable, but it is **not
502	geometric** — the same statement closes in an arbitrary category with pullbacks,
503	with every geometric hypothesis deleted (`I-1312`, `I-1316`). So what remains is the
504	invariance step producing a compatible family from a Galois-**invariant** `k'`-class
505	(`G1`, where the group action enters), the **scheme-level** quotient (`G2`, item 3),
506	and `k'`-side representability itself. `I-1280` states the pricing consequence and
507	`I-1312` corrects that item's overclaims.
508	
509	Present state of the four:
510	
511	1. **the descent test — LANDED.** `Picard/EtaleFieldCover.lean` proves
512	   `Spec k' ⟶ Spec k` is an étale cover for `k'/k` finite separable and that

12	/-!
13	# The tangent space of `Pic⁰_{C/k}` in its étale formulation
14	
15	The Kleiman §5 Thm. `thm:tgtsp` dimension development for `Scheme.Pic0SchemeEt C`
16	— the identity component of the scheme representing the **étale-sheafified**
17	relative Picard functor, which is the object the Jacobian headline binds
18	(`picardJacobianWitness`, `AlgebraicJacobian/Jacobian.lean`).
19	
20	## Why this file exists
21	
22	`Picard/Pic0AbelianVariety.lean` develops the same chain for `Pic0Scheme C`, the
23	identity component of the scheme representing the *unsheafified* `picSharp C`.
24	That development carries `[HasPicScheme C]`, a class with no instance whose only
25	producer is the conditional `picSchemeOfHasRationalPoint` — so it is a statement
26	about a *pointed* curve, and the headline's dimension leaf
27	`smoothOfRelativeDimension_genus_pic0Et` cannot consume it.
28	
29	## What this file corrects
30	
31	`Jacobian.lean` priced the étale dimension leaf as needing "the comparison of the
32	two Picard schemes, which is available only under a section" — i.e. exactly the
33	hypothesis the owner decision `I-0491` forbids the headline to carry. **That
34	pricing is wrong, and this file is the refutation.** Every engine of the
35	dual-number leg is quantified over an arbitrary functor and an arbitrary
36	`RepresentableBy`:
37	
38	* `Pic0.pointedDualNumberPointsEquivRepresentableFiber` and
39	  `pointedDualNumberPointsEquivAddKernel`
40	  (`Picard/Pic0DualNumberCocycle.lean`) take `(G, rep)` as arguments;
41	* `pointedDualNumberPointsEquivOfOpenImmersion` (`Picard/Pic0TangentSpace.lean`)
42	  takes an arbitrary morphism with open-immersion underlying map;
43	* `overDualNumberSectionEquivCotangentSpaceDual`
44	  (`Picard/TangentSpaceIdentitySection.lean`) takes an arbitrary `X` and section.
45	
46	`picSharp` entered only at the two *application* sites of
47	`Pic0AbelianVariety.lean`. Here the same engines are applied to
48	`(PicSharp.etaleSheaf C).obj` with `representableEt` — which is precisely the
49	`(G, rep)` pair they ask for, and which needs no rational point.
50	
51	## What is proved and what remains
52	
53	Proved outright, with no rational point and no `[HasPicScheme C]`:
54	`identitySection`, `pointedDualNumberPoints_equiv_cotangentSpaceDual`,
55	`pointedDualNumberPoints_equiv_relPicEtKernel` (the representability leg **against
56	`picEt`**), `cotangentSpaceDual_equiv_relPicEtKernel`, and
57	`finiteDimensional_cotangentSpace`.
58	
59	**What "axiom-clean" does and does not mean here**, since every declaration in this file
60	binds `[HasPicSchemeEt C]` and `#print axioms` on each reports only
61	`[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`. That is a statement about the *implications*: a
62	bound instance argument is never unfolded. At any real use site the unconditional
63	`instHasPicSchemeEt` fires, and its body is `(fgaPicardRepresentability C).1` — the
64	project's central `sorry`. So instantiating any declaration below at a bare curve reports
65	`sorryAx`. The honest phrasing, which the commit messages should have used: these add **no
66	new `sorry`**, and are axiom-clean *conditional on the `sorry`-backed `HasPicSchemeEt`
67	gate*. Nothing in this file is unconditional in the stronger sense of holding for a curve
68	today. Recorded after a fresh-context audit (`I-0988`).
69	
70	The dimension identity itself is stated as an **implication**. Its single antecedent is
71	`SemilinearCotangentComparisonEt`, which is clause for clause the same *shape* as the
72	`picSharp` side's own open residue
73	`Pic0.semilinearComparison_cotangentSpaceDual_h1Cok` (`Pic0AbelianVariety.lean`, a bare
74	`sorry`): same `∀ S`, same `∃ i j`, same bijectivity, same intertwining. This file adds
75	**no `sorry` of its own**; the antecedent is a named hypothesis, not a discharged
76	obligation.
77	
78	**It is one statement, but not the *same* statement — corrected after a fresh-context
79	audit (`I-0989`).** An earlier version of this paragraph said the étale formulation owes
80	"the same one statement the pointed formulation owes, and no more". The count is right and
81	the shape is right; the identification is not. The two antecedents compare **different
82	carriers**:
83	
84	* on the `picSharp` side the kernel is a kernel of `PicSharp.relPresheaf`, whose elements
85	  are honest invertible-sheaf classes (a quotient of `LineBundle.OnProduct`), and the
86	  residue is priced there as a Čech-to-invertible-sheaves comparison at a non-affine
87	  scheme;
88	* here the kernel description lands in a kernel of `(PicSharp.etaleSheaf C).obj` — the
89	  **sheafification** — so its elements are sheafification classes.
90	
91	Reusing the `picSharp` cocycle argument therefore needs a bridge from the sheafified
92	kernel back to the presheaf kernel at `Spec k[ε]`, and no such lemma exists in the
93	project. The two agree under a section (`picEtComparison_isIso_of_hasRationalPoint`), which
94	is exactly the hypothesis `I-0491` forbids and that this formulation exists to avoid. So
95	the étale antecedent additionally absorbs the sheafification-versus-presheaf step: not
96	extra `sorry`s and not a weakening, but unnamed cost inside a named hypothesis, named here.
97	
98	What this file does **not** do, stated plainly because it is easy to overread:
99	it does not close the headline leaf `smoothOfRelativeDimension_genus_pic0Et`.
100	That leaf needs, over and above the dimension count, the passage from a
101	tangent-space dimension to Mathlib's presentation-based
102	`SmoothOfRelativeDimension` (characterised by `Module.rank S Ω[S⁄R]`), plus
103	`Pic0Et.smooth` itself. Those are recorded on the leaf and are untouched here.
104	
105	## References
106	
107	Kleiman, "The Picard scheme" (arXiv:math/0504020), §5 Thm. `thm:tgtsp`.
108	Mumford, "Abelian varieties", §II.4 (the tangent-vector scaling).
109	-/

31	## The étale-sheafification route (owner decision of 2026-07-28)
32	
33	Kleiman §4 represents the **étale-sheafified** functor `Pic_{(C/k)ét}`, and
34	that is what this file's obligation is stated against —
35	`fgaPicardRepresentability`, over an **arbitrary** base field, with **no
36	hypothesis on `C(k)`**. The functor is built and its sheaf property proved in
37	`Picard/PicEtSheaf.lean` (`PicScheme.picEt`, `picEt_isSheaf_forget`), by
38	sheafifying the relative Picard presheaf for Mathlib's big étale topology
39	localised at `Spec k`.
40	
41	Why the sheafification is not optional. The plain relative functor
42	`picSharp C = T ↦ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)` is not representable over a
43	general field, so an unconditional `RepresentableBy` against `picSharp` is a
44	**false** statement, not merely an unproved one.
45	
46	**CITATION CORRECTED 2026-07-29 (`review-ajc`), by reading the source. The
47	conclusion above is right; the reason previously given for it was not.** This
48	paragraph used to say `picSharp` "is not even a Zariski sheaf (Kleiman §2

51	something else: "The **absolute** Picard functor `Pic_X` is never a separated
52	presheaf in the Zariski topology", proved with the `ℙ¹_X`/`O(1)` argument. That
53	is about `Pic_X`, **not** about the relative `Pic_{X/S} = picSharp`, which is
54	*defined* by quotienting out `Pic(T)` precisely to defeat that argument. What
55	Kleiman actually asserts about the relative functor is weaker (L1330): "Since
